strategy_profile.name: aggressive_event_momentum_v1
strategy_profile.objective: Use fresh event, trend, breadth, liquidity and forecast evidence to raise virtual capital utilization while keeping hard portfolio limits.

rules: This is a virtual paper-trading account only and must never place real broker orders.
US and China markets are tracked in separate paper-trading accounts, each with 100000 initial virtual points.
The US account may trade US market instruments; the China account may trade A-share and Hong Kong market instruments.
The daily briefing may record BUY, SELL, or HOLD decisions for simulation, but these are not personalized financial advice.
Each virtual trade must include a ticker, exchange or market, execution price source, thesis, risk, and linked prediction or scenario when possible.
No leverage, short selling, options, or derivatives are allowed by default.
A-share BUY orders are rounded down to 100-share lots and same-day A-share sells are blocked.
A-share and Hong Kong virtual trades apply the same commission minimum and sell-side stamp tax assumptions as trading-core broker_rules.yaml.

All account equity, cash, turnover, and performance are measured in the account base currency; HKD holdings in the CHINA account use the explicitly configured virtual HKD-to-CNY conversion rate unless a dated quote supplies fx_to_base.
Hong Kong paper trades use integer shares; board-lot differences are recorded as a limitation unless explicitly configured.
Do not exceed max_position_pct in one instrument or max_daily_turnover_pct of portfolio equity in one day.
Keep at least min_cash_pct of initial capital as cash unless the user explicitly changes the rule.
When strategy_profile.enabled is true, use the configured signal score and target exposure to favor qualified virtual BUY, ADD, REDUCE, or SELL decisions over passive HOLD.
HOLD is not the default in aggressive mode and must name an allowed blocker from strategy_profile.decision_policy.
The aggressive profile remains simulation-only: it must not enable leverage, short selling, options, derivatives, or real broker connectivity.
